identification.summary: Russia-affiliated espionage actor first publicly named by Microsoft Threat Intelligence on 2025-05-27, which assessed with high confidence that it has been active since at least April 2024 [S1]. The Dutch intelligence services AIVD and MIVD published the same activity under the name Laundry Bear, describing a previously unknown, very likely state-sponsored Russian actor [S2]. It relies mostly on stolen credentials and cookies and on bulk collection of email and files from cloud services [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: active since at least April 2024 [S1]. Dutch services date the Dutch police breach to September 2024 [S2][S3]. The 2026 US indictment alleges conspiracy conduct since at least 2023 [S4].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Void Blizzard; also LAUNDRY BEAR [S1]. The Dutch services use Laundry Bear [S2]. Microsoft notes target overlap with Forest Blizzard, Midnight Blizzard and Secret Blizzard, which it says suggests shared collection interests among parent organizations, not that the clusters are the same [S1]. Press reporting says the US indictment used both Void Blizzard and Laundry Bear names [S4][S6]. The CERT-UA / UAC-0190 alias in the imported record could not be verified in this research and is not added.

attribution.sponsor: Russia. Microsoft assesses with high confidence that the actor is Russia-affiliated [S1]. The Dutch AIVD and MIVD describe it as very likely state-sponsored [S2]. Reuters reports a US indictment (2026) alleging that Yutek-NN, a Russian technology firm, conducted cyber espionage at the Russian government's direction, and that the charged individual is a former FSB officer (2012-2017) who became a deputy director at Yutek [S4][S6]. The specific Russian state service tasking the actor is not stated in the sources gathered.
attribution.confidence: Microsoft: high confidence that the actor is Russia-affiliated [S1]. AIVD/MIVD: very likely state-sponsored [S2]. The US indictment allegations are unproven charges; the defendant pleaded not guilty [S4].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and joint research with AIVD and MIVD, with the FBI named as a continuing partner [S1]; Dutch intelligence investigation of the September 2024 police breach [S2]; US indictment of an alleged Yutek-NN deputy director, known only through press coverage (not the indictment text) [S4][S6].

objectives: Collection of intelligence for Russian strategic objectives; Microsoft notes disproportionate targeting of NATO member states and Ukraine [S1]. Dutch services say the actor seeks information on Western military procurement and production and on weapons deliveries to Ukraine [S2][S3][S5].

regions: NATO member states, especially those supporting Ukraine [S1]
targeting.notes: Microsoft lists government, defense, transportation, media, NGOs and healthcare primarily in Europe and North America, and adds communications, defense industrial base, education, IT and intergovernmental organizations since mid-2024 [S1]. In October 2024 several user accounts at a Ukrainian aviation organization were compromised [S1]. The Dutch services cite armed forces, governments, defense suppliers, civil society and IT/digital service providers [S2][S5]. Reuters reports the FBI identified at least 11 US companies hacked, which it considers a fraction of victims [S4].

capabilities.summary: Microsoft describes mostly unsophisticated initial access: password spray and stolen credentials and cookies, likely bought from infostealer ecosystems, used against Exchange Online and sometimes SharePoint Online [S1]. In April 2025 it ran an adversary-in-the-middle spear-phishing campaign against more than 20 NGO organizations in Europe and the US using a PDF lure with a malicious QR code and a typosquatted Entra sign-in domain; Microsoft assesses with the open-source Evilginx framework, and calls this a newly observed initial-access tactic for the actor [S1][S7]. After access it uses Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph APIs to enumerate and bulk-collect mailboxes (including shared mailboxes) and cloud files, in a few cases accessed Teams via the web client, and in some cases used the public AzureHound tool to map Entra ID [S1]. The Dutch services report cookie theft and replacement, brute forcing and phishing [S5]. The US indictment, per Reuters, alleges use of fake domains, VPNs and proxies [S4].

campaigns.name: Earliest activity assessed by Microsoft
campaigns.summary: Microsoft assesses activity since at least April 2024.

campaigns.name: Dutch police account compromise
campaigns.summary: Dutch services attribute a September 2024 breach of the Dutch police to Laundry Bear; work-related contact details were stolen and other theft could not be established. One secondary summary reports a pass-the-cookie technique against a police employee account; this was not confirmed in primary Dutch text reviewed [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Ukrainian aviation organization accounts
campaigns.summary: Several user accounts at a Ukrainian aviation organization were compromised, an organization that Seashell Blizzard had targeted in 2022.

campaigns.name: Entra AitM phishing of NGOs
campaigns.summary: Spear-phishing of more than 20 NGO organizations in Europe and the US using a fake European Defense and Security Summit PDF with a QR code leading to micsrosoftonline[.]com, assessed by Microsoft as Evilginx.

campaigns.name: Public disclosure by Microsoft, AIVD and MIVD
campaigns.summary: Microsoft publishes Void Blizzard; the Dutch services publish Laundry Bear.

campaigns.name: US prosecution of alleged Yutek-NN official
campaigns.summary: Reuters reports Denis Obrezko, extradited from Thailand after a November arrest, was indicted in Boston for conspiracy to commit computer fraud and abuse and pleaded not guilty; the indictment reportedly links Yutek-NN to Void Blizzard/Laundry Bear. Known only through press coverage.

diamond.adversary: Russia-affiliated espionage operators; alleged contractor link to Yutek-NN per press reporting of a US indictment [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: Credential and cookie theft, password spray, Evilginx-style AitM phishing, Exchange Online and Graph API bulk collection, AzureHound [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Typosquatted Microsoft-lookalike domains (micsrosoftonline[.]com, ebsumrnit[.]eu) [S1]; fake domains, VPNs and proxies per the reported indictment [S4].
diamond.victim: Government, defense, transportation, media, NGOs, healthcare, IT and defense suppliers in Europe and North America, plus Ukraine [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intelligence on Western support to Ukraine, military procurement and NATO decision-making [S1][S2][S5].
diamond.technology: Cloud identity and email (Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams) protected only by passwords or phishable MFA, and endpoints infected with infostealers [S1].

gaps: Which Russian state service tasks the actor is not stated in the sources gathered; Microsoft only says Russia-affiliated [S1].
The AIVD/MIVD page, CERT-UA article, Security Affairs, Cybersecurity Dive and The Register could not be opened (hosts blocked); Dutch details rely on search summaries and secondary coverage.
The US indictment text and DOJ press release were not accessed; Yutek-NN and Obrezko details come from Reuters wire reprints and RFE/RL and are allegations, with a pleaded not-guilty status [S4][S6].
UAC-0190 (CERT-UA) alias in the imported record is unverified; search returned nothing on it.
Pass-the-cookie detail for the police breach is from a secondary summary only.
No Void Blizzard activity after the April 2025 campaign was found in vendor reporting; current tempo is unknown.
Overlap with Forest, Midnight and Secret Blizzard is target overlap only; relationships to those clusters are not established [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Cloud identity and mail tenants (Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint/Teams) of defense, logistics, aviation and NGO partners are key terrain, because the actor collects mail and files in bulk there [S1]. STEP 2: The actor gains access with purchased credentials and cookies and AitM phishing rather than exploits, so identity hygiene, not patching, is the decisive variable [S1]. STEP 3: Template is infostealer credentials or Evilginx phish, then Exchange/Graph API enumeration, bulk mail and file collection, occasional AzureHound mapping [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued collection against NATO governments, defense suppliers and logistics firms for Ukraine-support information [S1][S2][S5]. MDCOA is targeting of air-traffic, transportation or supply-chain accounts to inform kinetic or sabotage planning; the sources show interest in aviation and arms-supply information but do not show that intent [S1][S5]. Candidate indicators: Microsoft lookalike domains, QR-code PDFs themed on defense events, anomalous token and AitM Entra alerts, non-owner mailbox access and bulk Graph API reads [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: feed Entra ID Protection risk detections (Attacker in the Middle, Password spray, Anomalous Token) and mailbox audit data from mission and contractor tenants into the operational picture [S1]. (2) Authorities: monitoring of partner and contractor tenants depends on contractual and legal arrangements; coordinate with DC3 and the DIB cybersecurity program rather than assuming access. (3) Mission assurance: enforce phishing-resistant MFA, conditional access and credential rotation after infostealer detections for accounts tied to logistics, aviation and procurement planning [S1]. (4) Coordination: sharing with allied partners, noting the Dutch services and FBI collaboration, and treating Ukraine-support supply-chain staff as priority protectees [S1][S2].
